notes: Account summary: Large regional bank, strong interest in moving chat and doc search onto dedicated inference to reduce TCO and meet residency requirements.
Primary motivators: predictable latency for customer-facing chat, deterministic throughput during peak hours (9-11am ET), vendor-managed security and audit trails.
POC ask: 2-week Dedicated POC (8x A100-equivalent) with synthetic + production replay traffic. Goal: verify latency SLOs and throughput guarantees under 100–150 concurrent sessions.
Latency SLO discussion (key):
- Coppergate wants explicit definitions for p50/p95/p99 across request types. They differentiate: non-streaming (full-response) vs streaming (time-to-first-byte + per-token interval).

- Desired targets discussed on 2026-03-02 call: non-streaming generation p95 <= 350ms for short chat prompts (avg 40 tokens), p99 <= 700ms. Streaming: TTFB p95 <= 120ms, steady-state per-token p95 <= 40ms. (These are customer targets — open to tuning with model choice/quantization.)

- Measurement alignment: customer expects client-side timing (browser or mobile SDK) to be source of truth for UX. Redwood and Coppergate to align on canonical instrumentation: server-side ingress timestamp, server-side first-byte, server-side per-token timestamps, plus client-reported TTFB. Need mapping doc explaining how to reconcile differences (clock drift, proxies).

- Important callouts from SE (Ravi): streaming SLO must explicitly state whether it measures time-to-first-byte (initial response) or time-to-first-token from model. Also define how partial tokens/continuations are treated for percentiles.
Throughput & reserved GPU planning notes:

- Baseline estimate: 8 GPUs for steady 100 concurrent chat sessions with batching + KV cache; with burst 12 GPUs to maintain p95 targets at peak traffic. Team requests Redwood capacity planning worksheet to validate concurrency assumptions.
- Caching expectations: prefix/KV caching could reduce backend compute by ~30% on repeat queries (their usage patterns show many repeated account-status prompts). Include cache warming plan in POC.
SLA negotiation points (legal):
- Coppergate requires latency SLOs in contract with credits if SLA missed more than 3x in a month. Redwood proposed service credits and a clause for configurable SLO tiers (standard vs premium).

- Legal wants explicit measurement sources and dispute resolution steps: Redwood metric dashboard + raw request logs (redacted). Need to confirm retention windows that satisfy Coppergate's audit policy.
POC test plan bullets (from drive doc):
- Run synthetic load to 150 qps (chat) with 40-token avg; measure p50/p95/p99 server vs client-side for both streaming and non-streaming modes.
- Re-run with production replay of 24 hours sampled traffic to capture tail behavior and burst profiles.
- Validate model fallback policy under GPU pressure and measure failover latency to a lower-cost variant.
Key quotes from stakeholders:
- Head of Digital Channels: "We cannot accept finger-pointing on latency — need one clear metric that maps to the customer experience."
- Platform lead: "If we can guarantee p95 for streaming TTFB, we'll prioritize Redwood for reserve capacity."
Action items (recent):
- SE to produce latency-measurement alignment doc (due 2026-03-12).
- AE (Aria) to coordinate legal handoff and request draft SLA template (in drive).
- Schedule POC kickoff for week of 2026-03-22 pending legal/finance approvals.
Risks and notes:
- Client-side timing vs server-side discrepancies: mobile operators add 50–120ms variance — requires conservative SLOs or edge routing policy.
- Cost sensitivity: Coppergate asks for committed monthly pricing with predictable overage bands; finance to sign off only after POC numbers show unit economics.
- Suggested Redwood play: offer a two-tier SLO (During POC metric baseline: informational SLO; Post-POC: contractual SLO with limited credits) to unblock procurement.
Misc links and artifacts: drive deck contains historical tail latency graphs, fireflies has full call transcript (ff-2026-03-02-az7k2).

- 'POC: 8->12 GPU scale test, 2 weeks'
